sources.name: Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD)
sources.affiliation_note: US think tank with a documented programmatic line on Iran, sanctions, and Middle East security policy; research and advocacy consistently support a hawkish foreign-policy agenda aligned with one side of regional conflicts, rather than nonpartisan analysis.

sources.name: Henry Jackson Society
sources.affiliation_note: UK think tank with a documented programmatic hawkish/interventionist foreign policy line; outputs consistently advocate one side of the conflicts and policy debates it covers rather than nonpartisan analysis.

sources.name: Meir Amit Intelligence and Terrorism Information Center
sources.affiliation_note: Staffed largely by former Israeli intelligence and military officials; outputs reflect the Israeli security establishment's perspective on conflict actors rather than independent nonpartisan research.

sources.name: Institute for National Security Studies (INSS)
sources.affiliation_note: Israeli think tank, institutionally affiliated with Tel Aviv University but historically staffed by former Israeli defence-establishment officials (IDF, Mossad); research reflects a programmatic alignment with the Israeli security establishment's positioning on conflict topics.

sources.name: Atlantic Council
sources.affiliation_note: US think tank funded substantially by NATO, NATO member governments, defence contractors, and foreign governments with direct stakes in the conflicts and policy debates it covers; outputs reflect a programmatic Atlanticist/NATO-aligned line.

sources.name: Russian International Affairs Council (RIAC)
sources.affiliation_note: Russian think tank institutionally linked to the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs; outputs reflect official Russian foreign-policy positioning rather than independent nonpartisan analysis.

sources.name: Valdai Discussion Club
sources.affiliation_note: Forum and publication functioning as a mouthpiece for the Russian foreign-policy elite; outputs consistently reflect official Russian state positioning on conflict topics rather than independent nonpartisan analysis.

sources.name: Stiftung Wissenschaft und Politik (SWP) — German Institute for International and Security Affairs
sources.independence_note: German foreign- and security-policy think tank, partly funded by the German federal government (Chancellery/Bundestag) but operating with academic research independence and no single programmatic line on conflict topics. Classified neutral: non-state-controlled editorial process, but not fully independent of state funding.

sources.name: Middle East Institute (MEI)
sources.independence_note: US academic institute focused on Middle East policy and scholarship; diverse funding base including governments and private donors with no single funder holding editorial control. Classified neutral: academic, non-state, no documented programmatic line on conflict topics.

sources.name: Razumkov Centre
sources.independence_note: Ukrainian think tank; non-state, academic-style research institute with no documented programmatic line beyond Ukrainian public-policy analysis. Classified neutral rather than fully independent given its national-policy focus.

sources.name: Rosa-Luxemburg-Stiftung
sources.affiliation_note: Rosa-Luxemburg-Stiftung is the political foundation affiliated with Die Linke. It receives the majority of its funding from the German federal budget, allocated through a parliamentary formula tied to party representation. Research and publications reflect a broadly democratic-socialist political perspective. Classified not independent, symmetric with kas.de/fes.de/boell.de/freiheit.org/hss.de — political-foundation affiliation is assessed identically regardless of which party it is tied to.

sources.name: Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung (FES)
sources.affiliation_note: Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung is the political foundation affiliated with the SPD (Sozialdemokratische Partei Deutschlands). It receives the majority of its funding from the German federal budget, allocated through a parliamentary formula tied to party representation. Research and publications reflect a broadly social-democratic political perspective. Classified not independent, symmetric with kas.de/rosalux.de/boell.de/freiheit.org/hss.de — political-foundation affiliation is assessed identically regardless of which party it is tied to.

sources.name: Heinrich-Böll-Stiftung
sources.affiliation_note: Heinrich-Böll-Stiftung is the political foundation affiliated with Bündnis 90/Die Grünen. It receives the majority of its funding from the German federal budget, allocated through a parliamentary formula tied to party representation. Research and publications reflect a broadly green/progressive political perspective. Classified not independent, symmetric with kas.de/rosalux.de/fes.de/freiheit.org/hss.de — political-foundation affiliation is assessed identically regardless of which party it is tied to.

sources.name: Friedrich-Naumann-Stiftung für die Freiheit
sources.affiliation_note: Friedrich-Naumann-Stiftung für die Freiheit is the political foundation affiliated with the FDP (Freie Demokratische Partei). It receives the majority of its funding from the German federal budget, allocated through a parliamentary formula tied to party representation. Research and publications reflect a broadly liberal/free-market political perspective. Classified not independent, symmetric with kas.de/rosalux.de/fes.de/boell.de/hss.de — political-foundation affiliation is assessed identically regardless of which party it is tied to.

sources.name: Hanns-Seidel-Stiftung (HSS)
sources.affiliation_note: Hanns-Seidel-Stiftung is the political foundation affiliated with the CSU (Christlich-Soziale Union). It receives the majority of its funding from the German federal budget, allocated through a parliamentary formula tied to party representation. Research and publications reflect a broadly Christian-conservative/Bavarian political perspective. Classified not independent, symmetric with kas.de/rosalux.de/fes.de/boell.de/freiheit.org — political-foundation affiliation is assessed identically regardless of which party it is tied to.

sources.name: Washington Examiner
sources.affiliation_note: Owned by Clarity Media Group (Philip Anschutz, a major Republican donor). Editorial positioning consistently conservative-aligned across opinion and news coverage.

sources.name: World Socialist Web Site (WSWS)
sources.affiliation_note: Published by the International Committee of the Fourth International / Socialist Equality Party; functions as a Trotskyist party platform rather than an independent newsroom.

sources.name: kath.net
sources.affiliation_note: Conservative-Catholic advocacy outlet; editorial line consistently promotes a programmatic religious-conservative position rather than independent reporting.

sources.name: Gesellschaft zur wissenschaftlichen Untersuchung von Parawissenschaften (GWUP)
sources.independence_note: German skeptics organisation; non-state, advocates for a pro-scientific-consensus position rather than nonpartisan reporting. Classified neutral: not state- or party-affiliated, but has a consistent advocacy stance on pseudoscience/paranormal claims.

sources.name: ESPN
sources.independence_note: Established sports media outlet (Disney/Hearst/NFL stake). Independent for general sports reporting; not independent for claims directly involving ESPN, Disney, broadcast rights, or partner leagues.

sources.name: Lawfare
sources.independence_note: Legal and national-security analysis publication; Brookings/Lawfare Institute context. Strong specialist source, treated as neutral (not institutionally independent) for politically contested security claims.

sources.name: Schweizerische Bundesbahnen
sources.affiliation_note: Swiss national railway company. Primary source for its own operations/documents; not independent for claims concerning the SBB itself.

sources.name: ResearchGate
sources.independence_note: Hosting/profile platform, not a publisher; performs no own quality control. Peer-review status lies with the individual paper.

sources.name: Council on Foreign Relations
sources.independence_note: US foreign-policy think tank and membership organization; treated as neutral for contested geopolitical claims (consistent with SWP/MEI).

sources.name: Deutschlandfunk Kultur
sources.independence_note: Public-service broadcaster (Deutschlandradio).

sources.name: Amnesty International Austria
sources.independence_note: Human-rights NGO with own research and advocacy mandate; institutionally independent, normatively human-rights positioned.

sources.name: Amnesty International Switzerland
sources.independence_note: Human-rights NGO with own research and advocacy mandate; institutionally independent, normatively human-rights positioned.

sources.name: Amadeu Antonio Stiftung
sources.affiliation_note: Advocacy foundation against right-wing extremism, largely publicly funded; party in the contested discourse on AfD/extremism claims. Not-independent is not a quality judgment (its research may be excellent) — it means it does not count as an independent threshold source on those claims, symmetric to how a mirrored right-leaning advocacy foundation would be treated.

sources.name: Wiener Zeitung
sources.affiliation_note: Owned 100% by the Republic of Austria (Wiener Zeitung GmbH); editorially self-managed but without the public-broadcaster governance buffer between state and newsroom. Official ≠ independent.

sources.name: American Presidency Project (UC Santa Barbara)
sources.independence_note: Academic primary database for US presidential/election statistics.

sources.name: earth.org
sources.independence_note: Environmental/climate NGO-style media outlet with advocacy orientation and aggregating character; treated as neutral rather than an independent authority for contested policy claims.

sources.name: Arbeitsmarktservice Österreich
sources.affiliation_note: Austrian Public Employment Service; official labour-market data. Not independent for claims concerning its own performance, policy role, or government labour-market policy.

sources.name: American Institute of Physics
sources.independence_note: Scientific publisher / professional physics organization; high-quality expert source. Individual article type and peer-review status must be checked; on domain level treated as secondary, not primary.

sources.name: Grenzwissenschaft-aktuell
sources.independence_note: German blog/outlet for fringe science and speculative topics; not treated as an established scientific source.

sources.name: The Bridge
sources.independence_note: Indian sports news outlet.

sources.name: Israelnetz
sources.affiliation_note: Christian pro-Israel media initiative; structurally positioned on Israel/Palestine and Middle East conflict claims.

sources.name: US Environmental Protection Agency
sources.affiliation_note: US federal environmental agency; primary source for EPA actions, regulatory documents, enforcement and datasets. Not independent for claims concerning US government policy, EPA decisions, or politically contested regulation.

sources.name: zentralplus
sources.independence_note: Regional Swiss news outlet for Central Switzerland; own reporting, limited weight for national or technical claims.

sources.name: News24
sources.independence_note: Established South African news outlet (Media24).

sources.name: iraqfootball.me
sources.independence_note: Topical blog on Iraqi football history; can provide context/leads but does not carry a rating threshold like an established editorial or archival source.

sources.name: ACLED
sources.independence_note: Armed Conflict Location & Event Data — conflict-event dataset with documented methodology; primary/data source for recorded conflict events, not automatically for political interpretation.

sources.name: Aargauer Zeitung
sources.independence_note: Belongs to CH Media (Wanner, sole ownership since 2026-04-01); when cited alongside luzernerzeitung.ch / schweizheute.ch / watson.ch / other CH-Media titles, account for owner concentration (not independent domains).

sources.name: Anadolu Agency
sources.affiliation_note: Turkish state news agency; usable as an agency/secondary source but not independent on Turkish government interests or geopolitical conflict situations (analogous to RT/TRT/CGTN).

sources.name: Alexandria Magazin
sources.independence_note: Small Austrian online magazine; editorial structure unclear.

sources.name: ZOiS Berlin
sources.independence_note: Publicly funded research institute on Eastern Europe; academically relevant but treated as neutral (not institutionally independent) on geopolitical claims, consistent with SWP/MEI/CFR.

sources.name: Clean Energy Wire
sources.independence_note: Non-profit specialist journalism portal on the energy transition and climate policy; thematically focused, editorially independent.

sources.name: Race to the WH
sources.independence_note: Election forecast/visualization portal.

sources.name: International Business Times UK
sources.independence_note: International news/business portal with aggregating character; not a load-bearing evidence source for scientific, medical or sensitive political claims.

sources.name: Einstein Foundation Berlin
sources.affiliation_note: Publicly funded science-promotion foundation; primary source for its own programs, funding decisions and institutional statements, not independent for assessments of its own activity or funded projects.

sources.name: medinfo-verlag.ch
sources.independence_note: Medical specialist publisher; individual content may be relevant but peer-review and evidence status must be checked per article. Not threshold-bearing at domain level.

sources.name: FemBio
sources.independence_note: Women's biography database/portal.

sources.name: Verfassungsblog
sources.independence_note: Legal-scholarship publication with academic collective editorship; suitable for legal analysis, not a primary source for court decisions themselves.

sources.name: Schweiz heute
sources.independence_note: National news portal of CH Media (editorial network ~350 journalists); belongs to CH Media (Wanner) — when cited alongside aargauerzeitung.ch / luzernerzeitung.ch / watson.ch / other CH-Media titles, account for owner concentration.

sources.name: FAIR
sources.affiliation_note: FAIR (Fairness & Accuracy in Reporting); left/progressive media-criticism advocacy outlet. Not independent, symmetric to right-leaning advocacy media/think tanks.

sources.name: egoFM
sources.independence_note: Radio-station blog; lifestyle/culture context, not threshold-bearing for political, scientific or technical claims.

sources.name: finanzen.net
sources.independence_note: Financial portal with news-aggregation character.

sources.name: Born's IT & Windows blog
sources.independence_note: Single-author IT/security blog; competent for IT context but no editorial control structure, not threshold-bearing.

sources.name: Tech Policy Press
sources.independence_note: Tech-policy specialist publication; editorially produced, thematically focused with policy-analysis orientation; treated as neutral consistent with other policy-analysis sources.

sources.name: futurism.com
sources.independence_note: Tech/science news portal with magazine and aggregation character; not a load-bearing source for scientific, medical or security-critical evidence.

sources.name: notevenpast.org
sources.independence_note: History publication portal (University of Texas at Austin, Dept. of History).

sources.name: Einstein-Website
sources.independence_note: Private Einstein biography website (single operator).

sources.name: bahnonline.ch
sources.independence_note: Railway-enthusiast/specialist portal; not an established editorial news outlet.

sources.name: investing.com
sources.independence_note: Financial aggregator/market-data portal.

sources.name: 270toWin
sources.independence_note: Election forecast/visualization portal aggregating polls and forecasts.

sources.name: NDR
